scope: Internal native evidence for Ebisumaru sweets-challenge hide detection, bomb emission and bomb-task completion; not copied to the website.

proofs.scope: File42 root callback ABI, phase4 hide predicate and native positions, phase6 bomb coordinates and RNG ordering, bomb callback ground gate/children/retirement, and D_801FC60C ownership consequences.

functions.name: func_08001954_6F1B64
functions.abi: void (task pointer in a0, object pointer in a1); entry assembly confirms both arguments despite misleading decompiler typing
functions.observed: Phase 4 reads the live D_801FC60C player object after local-camera work. It tests four signed X/Z centers [(80,-49),(49,48),(-96,99),(-62,-23)] and hides if any has single-precision sqrt(dx*dx+dz*dz)<14.0 and playerY+15.0<-40.0. No form, action, line-of-sight or target-field gate was found. If exposed, selects animation 2 at rate 0.25 and flags 1, sets phase 6 and phase frame 0; normal epilogue increments the frame unless the sweet-allocation early return bypasses it. Hidden retraction follows the frame-120 gate. Phase 6 residues 1 and 21 emit at most one bomb per matching callback: residue 1 uses two RNG(20) samples minus 10 and adds them to current player X/Z; residue 21 uses two RNG(200) samples minus 100, with X based on clamp(playerX,-112,112)/1.2 in double precision then converted to float, and Z based on current player Z. Both write Y=50. The callback also owns local camera, player state and statistics backup/restoration paths; it is not a pure hide query.

functions.name: func_08000E2C_6F103C
functions.abi: void (task pointer in a0, object pointer in a1)
functions.observed: In its active phase, waits for task status +0x68 bit 0x20 to clear, then creates two native explosion children and retires. The callback does not perform target selection; root emission chooses bomb position earlier.

functions.name: D_801FC60C_5B851C
functions.observed: The shared current-player object pointer supplies phase4 hide detection and phase6 bomb coordinates to the root callback. The same callback has local camera, player-state and statistics backup/restoration work, so substituting the global position for the whole callback is not a read-only target redirection.

limitations: The visual description of the native detector as a tall bomb-dropper is an inference from its central hide-check and bomb-emission behavior; no model identity is established by this proof.

Hide testing uses native single-precision subtraction, square root and strict comparisons. The documented threshold is not guaranteed bit-identical to a squared-distance rewrite at floating-point boundaries.
Evidence is static decompilation/disassembly. No additional native callback invocation, gameplay run, or live multiplayer test was performed.
